operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names (Apartment_Buildings, View_Unit_Status) and CamelCase columns; must double-quote identifiers and compare case-insensitively.
All tables tiny (7-20 rows); no huge-table sampling needed, but read_schema must still work with max_rows_per_table.
DATETIME columns store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no T, no timezone); Date fuzzer template must parse this.
View_Unit_Status PK is status_date alone (DATETIME) — a date column as sole PK; composite-PK member rule does not apply, single-PK inf max_l0 applies.
Apartment_Facilities has composite PK (apt_id, facility_code) with apt_id also an FK to Apartments — composite-PK member + FK child overlap.

Apartments.building_id FK values (808,624,225,744,191) do NOT match Apartment_Buildings.building_id samples (133,153,191,196,225) — only 191/225 overlap; FK parent set is small (15) and child distinct is 9, so ties/duplicates expected.
room_count declared CHAR(5) but stores integer-looking text ('7','5','8') — String fuzzer with int-like element expansion applies.
available_yn declared BIT, storage integer 0/1 — Bit fuzzer, not Bool.
gender_code CHAR(1) stores 'Male'/'Female'/'Unknown' (length > 1) — declared length contradicts stored values; String length range from elements will be [4,8].
building_phone VARCHAR(80) has varied formats ('(948)040-1064x387','915-617-2408x832','681.772.2454','1-724-982-9507x640') — String fuzzer will contaminate these.
building_address contains embedded newlines and commas — String fuzzer charset excludes newline, so fresh values differ structurally.
No dangling FKs, no self-references, no missing parents; all parent_exists=true.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on DATETIME columns: template inferred from first parsable element = '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 1970..2007 for status_date, 2016..2018 for booking dates).

Date fuzzer p-inversion: p=0.2 means element returned w.p. 0.2, fresh dates w.p. 0.8 — most generated dates are fresh uniform in the narrow original range, so date predicates like 'between 2016 and 2017' stay plausible but ties to specific originals are lost.

Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs (building_id, apt_id, guest_id, apt_booking_id): range [-10^4,10^4] (scale=4 default for bare INTEGER? actually scale from args absent -> scale=0 -> [-1,1]? upstream default scale=4 when no args) — likely wide range, so PK values far from originals; joins on PK still work because FK draws from parent.
String fuzzer on names/addresses/phones: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with 50% contamination — implausible for LIKE '%Court%' or exact-name predicates -> FN.

String fuzzer on low-cardinality enums (apt_type_code 3 distinct, booking_status_code 2, facility_code 4, gender_code 3): elements dominate (p=0.2 fresh), so enum equality mostly preserved; but contamination can corrupt 'Studio'->'StudioXY' -> occasional FN.
Bit fuzzer on available_yn: 0/1 with p=0.2 element, else random 0/1 — fine.

FK consistency: Apartment_Bookings.apt_id drawn from Apartments.apt_id final values; View_Unit_Status.apt_booking_id from Apartment_Bookings.apt_booking_id — joins preserved, but child distinct counts (10,12) vs parent sizes (15) mean duplicates/ties appear.

View_Unit_Status PK = status_date alone: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate dates; Date fuzzer with max_l0=inf (single PK) draws fresh dates each row, so PK collisions rare -> table keeps ~n rows.

Apartment_Facilities composite PK (apt_id, facility_code): apt_id is FK child (drawn from Apartments, ~15 values) and facility_code String (4 elements) — PK dedup keeps first occurrence, so at most 15*4=60 distinct pairs; with n~30-200 many rows dropped -> small table, ties on apt_id expected.
Known FN driver: String fuzzer on building_short_name/full_name/address/phone destroys exact-match and LIKE predicates; Date fuzzer on booking_start/end_date loses original date ties.

Known FP driver: missing duplicates — original Apartments.building_id has 9 distinct over 15 rows (duplicates), but FK draw with replacement from 15 parents gives similar multiplicity; View_Unit_Status.apt_id 12 distinct over 20 rows, FK draw may under/over-represent.
